chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abi Jameelah, who said:

I saw in Fars a woman who had two heads and two chests in one hip, married, and this one would be jealous of this one and this one of this one. He said, and others narrated to us that he saw a man like that, and they were weavers, both working together on one loom.
ai.seo_question: What is the description of the physical anomaly of the woman with two heads in Fars according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of *khuntha* (hermaphroditism) jurisprory by documenting a rare physical anomaly in Fars where a woman possessed two heads and chests but shared one hip, leading to unique marital dynamics of mutual jealousy. The detail that both individuals were weavers working on a single loom underscores their functional unity and capacity for independent action, which is crucial for determining inheritance and legal status in Shia fiqh. This case serves as a primary example of how physical duality within a single body challenges and clarifies the boundaries of gender classification in Islamic law.
